theorem_bound.label: W1 theorem: no counterfeiter beats
theorem_bound.source: A. Molina, T. Vidick, J. Watrous. Optimal counterfeiting attacks and generalizations for Wiesner's quantum money. TQC 2012, LNCS 7582, 45-64. arXiv:1202.4010v1; MVW2012 Theorem 1; https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4010
theorem_bound.note: ideal game W1 only: one note, two outputs, exact verifier, no oracle

lower.label: Achieved by an explicit channel (exact)
lower.note: exact rational arithmetic: a rigorous LOWER end

upper_certified.label: No channel exceeds (certified dual)
upper_certified.formula: Tr Y′ with Y′ ⊗ 1 − G_n ≻ 0 verified by exact LDLᵀ
upper_certified.note: SCS dual rounded to dyadics, shifted by δ = 1.82e-12; weak duality

upper_independent.label: Independent exact check (lane D)
upper_independent.note: separate code path: own rational G_n and exact PSD test; imports nothing from lane C

numerical.label: Numerical SDP (SCS)
numerical.note: primal 0.5625, dual 0.5625; floating point, not a proof

hardware.label: Quantum hardware

attack_result.quantum_channel_description: Breidbart measurement followed by the most-likely-to-pass resend.
attack_result.verifier_rule: exact projective BB84 verifier on every position; both candidates must pass

assumptions: one genuine note; the counterfeiter returns two candidate notes; the bank verifies both in the secret bases
Monte Carlo draws a FRESH secret note per trial (never repeated shots of one note)
data.simulator_caveat: A simulator's state is classical data that can be copied freely; nothing here demonstrates physical no-cloning. Only the modelled quantum register is simulated.
